about: Generated tables of docs/benchmarks.md, rendered by docs/scripts/render_benchmarks.py. 'runs' holds the consolidated EC2 runs: 'label' and 'rows' are copied from each run folder's consolidated.json, 'chain' from the end-to-end table of its CONSOLIDATED.md (with en dashes and ×), 'source' is the folder in this repository and 'caption' is the short name the page prints. 'more' holds runs outside the consolidated benchmark, all in the Docker VM ('more_label'), each group with its own source. Units: microseconds per document (rows; pyroid_us is one thread on CPython 3.15t, pyroid_us_8_threads a pool of 8, incumbents one process on CPython 3.13) and seconds per run (chain). Every value is a string copied from the source, never computed.

more.title: pyroid.metrics: ROUGE, BLEU and chrF
more.note: Milliseconds for the whole workload, median of the runs (a single run for the reference libraries on 100k pairs). Every row was first checked identical to the 1-process reference. The reference libraries ran in 1 process and in 8 forked processes, pyroid in one process with threads=1 and threads=8. CPython 3.13, release wheel; other work kept the load average between 4 and 19. ROUGE scores CNN/DailyMail lead-3 against the highlights with rouge1/2/L/Lsum (the 100k pairs are the 11,490 pairs repeated). BLEU and chrF use WMT21 segments, the first reference and default settings.

more.title: pyroid.json_repair
more.note: Single documents, best time per call, json_repair 0.64.5 on CPython 3.12 (3.15t was within ±10%). Release wheel; other work kept the load average between 16 and 24.

more.title: pyroid.json_repair: batches
more.note: Documents per second over 10,000 broken documents of about 1.2 KB, on free-threaded CPython 3.15t with the GIL off. The shared, loaded VM limits the 8-thread rows.

more.title: Languages: FineWeb-2 filters and MinHash
more.note: µs per document over 1,000 documents per language (each FineWeb-2 slice four times), median of 5 runs (2 for datatrove). Every timed document was first checked for the same keep/drop, reason and signatures. The filters are FineWeb-2's chain (Gopher repetition, FineWeb quality, Gopher quality) with each language's settings; MinHash computes FineWeb-2's signatures. datatrove's 8 processes are a warmed fork Pool(8). CPython 3.13, release wheel, load average 6 to 16. Chinese and Japanese use datatrove's Python tokenizers (python_tokenizer=True), so they run at those tokenizers' speed, on the calling thread.
more.footnote: \* An outlier: in this run pyroid was slower with 8 threads than with 1 while the load rose. It needs a rerun before it can be quoted.

more.title: More datatrove steps
more.note: Each datatrove step alone on the FineWeb dev slice, in one process and in a warmed multiprocessing.Pool(8), against pyroid's native call at 1 and 8 threads. Medians of 5 runs for pyroid and 2 for datatrove; release wheel, CPython 3.13, taskset -c 0-7, load average about 8 (about 22 for the URL filter). Where datatrove wasn't measured at 8 processes, the 8-thread speedup is against one process.
more.source: a one-off run on 2026-11-06, whose scripts are not in the repository

more.title: datatrove's FineWeb pipeline with pyroid's steps swapped in
more.note: Whole runs on the FineWeb dev slice (10,000 documents unless noted): wall seconds, and user+sys CPU seconds including children, from bash's `time`. CPython 3.13, release wheel, taskset -c 0-7. The VM was heavily shared (load average 18 to 30), which slows stock datatrove the most, so each ratio comes from a pair of runs in the same minute (stock, then pyroid). pyroid's runs include datatrove's executor phases, worker start-up, Parquet IO and loading the 125 MiB model; `pyroid clean` includes interpreter start-up, IO and writing both outputs. Every output has datatrove's per-document digest.
